origin.description: The function mcmc is used to create a Markov Chain Monte Carlo object. The input data are taken to be a vector, or a matrix with one column per variable. An mcmc object may be summarized by the summary function and visualized with the plot function.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object that may be coerced to an mcmc object
Further arguments to be passed to specific methods

origin.details: as.mcmc.default returns x unchanged when x is already an mcmc object; otherwise it builds one with mcmc(x). If start, end, and thin are omitted in that construction, the chain starts at iteration 1 with thinning interval 1.
origin.value: An mcmc object: numeric sample values with mcpar attribute c(start, end, thin).
origin.example: n <- 2000; i <- seq_len(n); x <- cbind(sin(i/3)+0.2*cos(i), cos(i/5)+0.01*i, rep(2, n)); obj <- as.mcmc(x); cat(start(obj), end(obj), thin(obj), paste(format(obj[1,], digits=5), collapse=" "), "\n")

translation.description: Coerce a vector or matrix to an Mcmc chain object. Existing Mcmc objects are returned unchanged.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector, matrix, or Mcmc object.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Optional start, end, and thin arguments forwarded to mcmc construction when x is not already Mcmc.

translation.details: as.mcmc.default returns x unchanged when x is already an mcmc object; otherwise it builds one with mcmc(x). If start, end, and thin are omitted in that construction, the chain starts at iteration 1 with thinning interval 1.
translation.value: An Mcmc instance with data (vector or matrix) and start, end, and thin fields matching R mcpar.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from coda.as_mcmc import as_mcmc

n = 2000
i = np.arange(1, n + 1, dtype=float)
x = np.column_stack((np.sin(i / 3) + 0.2 * np.cos(i), np.cos(i / 5) + 0.01 * i, np.full(n, 2.0)))
obj = as_mcmc(x)
row = np.asarray(obj.data)[0]
print(obj.start, obj.end, obj.thin, " ".join(f"{v:.5f}" for v in row))
